title: Final meta-model experiment summary
metric: macro significant three-choice accuracy (gap>=0.05 & win_rate>=0.7 & non_overlap)

regression_per_dataset_baseline.description: 15 models, one per dataset, 600 train rows each, predict log(mean_loss)

regression_global_shared.description: 1 model on all 9000 train rows, dataset identity features, predict log(mean_loss)

winner_classification_per_dataset.description: Pairwise feature differences + binary win/lose classifier + triple vote, one model per dataset

winner_classification_global_shared.description: 1 shared pairwise classifier on all 9000 train rows (200k subsampled pairs), dataset identity

best_overall.setting: 1 model, 9000 train rows, 122 features (full + dataset identity), 300 trees depth 16, predict log(mean_loss)

key_conclusions: 1. Baseline (per-dataset regression) best: XGBoost 78.33%, ExtraTrees 77.78% — trees dominate.
2. Shared model helps ExtraTrees: 77.78% -> 82.11% (+4.33pp) by pooling all 9000 rows.
3. OLS/linear regression is weak (31-61%), confirming the task is nonlinear.
4. Winner classification (direct ABC) with gradient_boosting: 74.85% per-dataset — does NOT beat regression.
5. Winner classification global trees are surprisingly weak (56-62%) — pairwise approach hurts trees in global setting.
6. MLP classification (72.31% global) beats MLP regression (60.31% global) — direct winner prediction helps MLP but not enough to beat tree regression.
7. The original 63.50% was wrong due to: (a) no significance filter (+9pp), (b) suboptimal setting (+4pp). Corrected best: 82.11%.
8. Per-dataset ExtraTrees classifier still running; single-dataset test showed 83.18% on bigram, but macro across all 15 may be lower.
